s1.syndrome_frame: Acute collapse with recurrent ventricular arrhythmias
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Collapsed at home
Received chest compressions from her husband
Recovered consciousness at home
Vital signs were normal on admission
Physical examination was unremarkable
ECG showed sinus rhythm with normal QRS and QT intervals
ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes
Short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds
Serum electrolyte levels were normal
Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac function and structure
Emergency coronary angiography showed no evidence of obstructive coronary artery disease
Genetic testing revealed a variant of unknown significance in the RyR2 gene

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with a short-coupling interval, which is characteristic of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT). The patient's normal cardiac function and structure, as well as the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Familial polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: While the patient has a variant of unknown significance in the RyR2 gene, the clinical presentation is more consistent with CPVT.

rejected.label: Ryanodine receptor type 2 mutation-related arrhythmias
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation is more specific to CPVT than a general diagnosis related to RyR2 mutations.

rejected.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
rejected.why: The patient's ECG findings and clinical presentation suggest a more specific diagnosis than idiopathic ventricular fibrillation.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac function and structure, which is not consistent with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's ECG showed normal QT intervals, which is not consistent with long QT syndrome.

rejected.label: Early repolarization syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's ECG did not show the characteristic J-point elevation of early repolarization syndrome.

rejected.label: Brugada syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's ECG did not show the characteristic ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V3, which is diagnostic of Brugada syndrome.
